title: Single addition in a probabilistic program
statement:
Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register program with $m$ natural-number registers, state set $\Lambda$, and oracle, and fix an input $x$ and register bound $B$. Let $j,y,R$ be register indices with $j
e y$, $j
e R$, and $R
e y$. Suppose the instruction at state $test$ compares registers $j$ and $y$, going to $ex$ when they are equal and to $i_1$ otherwise; at $i_1$ it increments register $R$ and goes to $i_2$, and at $i_2$ it increments register $j$ and returns to $test$. For any rational $q$ and register valuation $v$ bounded by $B$, assume $v(j)\le v(y)$ and $v(R)+(v(y)-v(j))\le B$. If the configuration at $ex$ with register $R$ increased by $v(y)-v(j)$ and register $j$ set to $v(y)$ has probabilistic semantics of acceptance probability $q$ under the register bound $B$, then the configuration at $test$ with valuation $v$ has the same semantics and acceptance probability.
hypotheses_covered: The program $A$, oracle, input $x$, and bound $B$ are fixed
Every register value of $v$ is at most $B$
The specified configuration at $ex$ has probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $q$ under bound $B$
